result.title: What Stays in the Picture? From Redundant Instructions to Dependency-Aware Image Editing
result.summary: We introduce complex redundant-instruction image editing, where a single request specifies multiple objects, their attributes, and spatial relations while revising or canceling earlier editing requirements. Direct editing can fail to recover this intent, while splitting the request into successive steps can preserve obsolete edits and visual errors. Our key insight is to resolve the revision history into a final editing target that jointly guides planning and verification, so that obsolete requests do not become visual edits. Based on this insight, CRIE-Agent learns to consolidate revisions into object-level final intent and executes the retained objects in reference-first blocks, establishing referenced objects before their dependents. Verification then guides complete re-execution from the source image, with conditional layout hints, preventing visual errors from failed attempts from being carried into subsequent ones. We also construct CRIE-S, a benchmark containing 10,000 complex and redundant editing instructions with exact final intent annotations. Across five image-editing backends on CRIE-S, CRIE-Agent raises complete editing success from 0% under direct editing to 27.5--50.0%.

AI.brief_summary: 研究「复杂冗余指令图像编辑」：CRIE-Agent 先将多次修订的指令归并为对象级最终意图，再按依赖关系分块执行（先建立被引用对象），并在验证失败时从源图整段重执行，同时构建含 1 万条标注数据的 CRIE-S 基准。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「修订历史→最终意图」的状态归并、依赖排序执行与「验证触发回滚并弃用旧尝试」的机制，可能为 LVR 中作废证据的丢弃、错误中间状态的清除与停止/重试决策提供概念参照；但该方法属图像编辑智能体流程，与 latent 推理状态的关系需核查。
